posts.text: a year ago today. i didn't notice until my phone showed me a photo. i looked at it, felt something small, and went back to making lunch. that's the whole story.
i still sleep on my side of the bed. nobody's on the other side. i just can't make myself move over.
cried in the shower this morning, then made a really good breakfast. both things were true. i think that's what healing actually looks like.
someone asked how i'm doing and i said fine, and for the first time it wasn't a lie. it also wasn't true. it was just the closest word.
i hope whoever you're with now knows you hum when you cook. i hope they think it's as good as i did.
how does someone know you for four years and then decide they don't. what did they see that i can't.
i keep thinking about the version of that last fight where i just said "i'm scared" instead of everything else i said.
went on a walk with no podcast, no music. just me and my thoughts. they were quieter than i expected. that's new.
the kitchen is so quiet at night now. i never noticed how much noise another person makes just by existing.
3am is the hardest. the rest of the day i have things to do. at 3am there's just the ceiling and everything i didn't say.
i don't know if i miss them or i miss having someone to text about small things. both, probably. i'm allowed both.
i typed "i'm sorry" and stared at it for twenty minutes. i don't even know what i'd be apologizing for. i deleted it.
you don't get to say "i'll always care about you" on your way out the door. that's not caring. that's guilt looking for a softer word.
went to our old restaurant with a friend. ordered something new. it was fine. the place was just a place.
i was so busy being right that i forgot to be kind. i'd trade every argument i won for one more ordinary sunday.
started learning to cook the things they used to make for me. it's not the same. it's mine, though.
i stopped checking if they'd seen my stories. not because i healed. because i got tired. maybe that counts.
everyone wants me to be angry. i keep trying. mostly i just miss the way you said my name when you were half asleep.
the worst part was how calm they were. like they'd been practicing the goodbye for weeks while i was still planning a trip.
first time laughing at something on tv without immediately thinking "i should send them this." small. huge.
you left a sweater here. i'm not going to give it back and i'm not going to wear it. it just lives in the closet now, like a question.
bought a new set of sheets. it sounds stupid. it's the first thing in this apartment that was never ours.
i got through the whole day. work, groceries, dishes. i don't remember any of it. i think that's what people mean by functioning.
made it to noon without crying today. i'm counting it.
i hope you're doing well. i hope you sometimes wonder if i am. i'm not sending this. i'm just glad it's out of my chest.
found the playlist you made me. listened to the whole thing in the car in the driveway. didn't go inside for an hour.

replies.text: the "went back to making lunch" part got me. that's the goal, i think.
i can't imagine a year from now. but it helps to know someone got there.
i did this for months. one night i just rolled over and it was fine. it'll happen.
this is the kindest thing i've read all week.
sometimes they didn't see anything. sometimes it's not about you at all. that's not comforting yet. it will be.
needed this today. thank you for saying it plainly.
you don't have to be angry. you're allowed to miss them and still not go back.
"the closest word." yeah. that's exactly it.
the fridge hum. i know that one.
